name: A higher ceiling primes freedom

direction.note: The study used 8 ft and 10 ft ceilings.

claim: Students in a 3.05 m room felt more freedom and less confinement, and thought more abstractly, than students in a 2.44 m room.
caveat: The effect showed only when the ceiling height was made noticeable; it measures felt freedom and thought style, not pleasure; US students only.

sources.title: Meyers-Levy and Zhu 2007, The influence of ceiling height, Journal of Consumer Research 34(2)
